currentContext.expansion: ADSL is an asset-light IT services business, and its expansion narrative is about footprint, partnerships, platforms and capability rather than plants or capacity. Geographic expansion is being pursued into newer geographies to increase addressable markets: the Company is evaluating partnerships in Japan, has established new partnerships in Mauritius to address opportunities in Mauritius and Africa, and continues to explore inorganic growth opportunities globally; the stated strategy also includes continued expansion across Japan and EMEA markets. Strategic global partnerships are being built with leading technology players - the recent addition of IBM as a strategic partner has already contributed to a large FMCG opportunity, with several additional opportunities being pursued through that collaboration. The sales and delivery engine has been expanded through senior sales leadership added in the US, a broader sales organisation, a new leader for the India managed services business, a refreshed digital presence and a global implementation of Salesforce for lead tracking, pipeline management and sales governance. Platform build-out continues around Digital Desk, the proprietary low-code/no-code enterprise service management platform, which now manages more than 6 million support tickets annually at an average first-time resolution rate of approximately 87%, while the AIM 360 cybersecurity framework has been extended through an assessment platform aligned with NIST-based industry controls and computer-vision applications are being expanded beyond smart cities into enterprise environments. Capability expansion includes training more than 100 key resources in AI, evaluating multiple AI platforms, assessing voice-to-text and text-to-voice technologies for virtual AI agents, and developing new business models and innovative pricing structures. The Company has defined a clear roadmap for the next three to five years aligned with its longer-term ambition to build a business ten times its current scale, and states that it strategically increased leverage by securing additional financing facilities during the year to fund its long-term project pipeline and accelerate group-level growth. No plant, capacity or rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this material.

risks.risk: Volatile global outlook - macroeconomic, geopolitical and currency exposure
risks.note: Given its global footprint, diversified service portfolio and increasing participation in large transformation programmes, the Company is exposed to macroeconomic, geopolitical, regulatory, cybersecurity, delivery, talent and contract-management risks. Interest-rate movements, currency fluctuations, trade and tariff pressures, geopolitical conflict and energy-price volatility can influence customer spending, delivery costs and supply-chain stability across markets. Mitigated through quarterly management reviews, internal audits, proactive risk monitoring, supply-chain de-risking and operating discipline across business units.

risks.risk: Technology obsolescence and execution risk from rapid technology-led change
risks.note: Developments in Industry 4.0, agentic AI, connected infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity and digital engineering require continuous investment in skills, platforms and delivery models - technology-led change presents both opportunity and execution risk. Mitigated through structured technology-practice plans, R&D investment across geographies, expanding AI and cybersecurity capabilities and continuous team training.

risks.risk: AI governance, privacy, data-security, ethical-use and accountability risk
risks.note: AI is a defining growth opportunity but organisations that scale AI without adequate controls may expose sensitive information, create operational vulnerabilities or weaken decision governance. The Company is addressing this through AI training, internal policy development, responsible solution design and a formal AI usage framework aligned with its AI-first strategy, and is refining its AI governance policy.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity - one of the most critical risks for a managed service provider
risks.note: As the Company executes larger and more complex contracts it must protect customer environments and its own; it strengthens data protection, operational resilience, contractual safeguards and cyber-insurance coverage, supported by 24x7x365 monitoring of IT assets with leading tools, weekly security alerts and awareness checklists, controlled access and device binding, continuous patching, periodic vulnerability scanning of Digital Desk and Company websites, and continuous review of customer contracts for security obligations, risk allocation and insurance adequacy.

risks.risk: Compliance risk across multiple countries, including data protection
risks.note: Operating across multiple countries, non-compliance with legal, regulatory, labour, tax, data-protection and contractual requirements may result in legal exposure, financial penalties, operational disruption or reputational impact. Managed through defined ownership across sales, business units and corporate functions, periodic monitoring of regulatory changes, third-party specialists in selected jurisdictions, maintenance of certifications such as ISO, CMMI and PinkVERIFY, upgraded core platforms (SAP, Salesforce) and preparation for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.

risks.risk: Delivery risk and receivables / payment delays
risks.note: Delivery risk arises when service commitments, quality standards, response timelines or customer expectations are not met in a highly competitive managed-services market where customers expect continuous improvement, automation-led efficiency and measurable value. Mitigated through shift-left automation, analytical dashboards, disciplined pricing, delivery governance and active service monitoring. Payment delays remain a global operational concern, with the finance team managing receivables through structured follow-up and cash-flow discipline.

Risk may arise from unclear scope, changing customer expectations, complex delivery dependencies or evolving commercial terms; mitigated by standardising contract structures where appropriate, strengthening contract administration, improving understanding of customer environments and continuously refining contracts in line with service obligations and risk-allocation requirements.

risks.risk: Employee-related risk - attrition and specialised skill scarcity in a talent-driven business
risks.note: As a service-centric, talent-driven organisation, the ability to attract, develop and retain specialised talent is essential to competitiveness; attrition, skill scarcity and changing workforce expectations can affect delivery continuity and cost efficiency. Mitigated through cross-training, global and domestic recruitment models, collaboration with internal and external recruiters, leadership strengthening, skill-development programmes and close delivery oversight.

one-line thesis: Allied Digital achieved record revenue (Rs. 968 Cr, +20% YoY) and resolved critical audit qualifications regarding inter-corporate loans, clearing the path for institutional confidence. Growth is pivoting toward high-margin Enterprise AI and Managed Services, with a robust Rs. 2,000 Cr+ government pipeline in Maharashtra expected to rebound in FY27 despite Q4 delays caused by geopolitical equipment cost volatility.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs. 968 Cr (+20% YoY), Q4 run-rate >Rs. 1,000 Cr annualized. EBITDA: Rs. 112 Cr (+14% YoY), Margin 11% (impacted by one-offs). PAT: Rs. 36 Cr (+10% YoY) vs Rs. 32 Cr prior; Reported PAT suppressed by one-time ECL provision (~Rs. 36 Cr) but aided by Rs. 21 Cr deferred tax asset benefit. Order Book: Q4 wins Rs. 166 Cr; Pipeline includes Rs. 2,000 Cr+ (Maharashtra), two Rs. 600 Cr contracts, and rebid of Rs. 250 Cr Western Railway project. Net Debt: Inter-corporate loans of Rs. 112 Cr converted to equity; remaining Rs. 5-6 Cr non-interest loans now interest-bearing to comply with Sec 186.
guidance: Revenue growth: 20-25% YoY for FY27. Margins: Target 12.5-13% short-term, 15% long-term (driven by AI/Automation). Order inflow: Strong pipeline with major awards expected in Q2/Q3 FY27. Capex/Commissioning: Mumbai project (Rs. 150-200 Cr) to commission in 9 months followed by 5-year O&M.
order book & pipeline: Q4 new orders/renewals: Rs. 166 Cr. Key wins: Pune City Surveillance, Premier Pharma client, Deep Sea Oil Drilling managed services. Pending/Probable: Mumbai Govt contract (Rs. 150-200 Cr, announcement imminent), Western Railway rebid (Rs. 250 Cr total, expected July), Two Maharashtra state contracts (Rs. 600 Cr each), Noida Smart City.
segment / subsidiary detail: Services: +21% YoY (targeting 75-80% of mix for annuity visibility). Solutions: +17% YoY (strategic entry point). Enterprise Customers: +31% YoY. Government: -6% YoY (temporary delay due to war-induced equipment cost spikes and tender processing lags); expected rebound FY27.
growth verticals / optionality: Agentic AI architecture deployment reducing Level 1 support headcount by 20-25%; Smart City sensor/edge AI integration; Conversion of Solutions projects into 5-year Managed Services annuities; Geographic expansion in North America, Latin America, and Africa.
margins & cost dynamics: Current EBITDA margin 11% pressured by one-time ECL provisions and elevated direct expenses (equipment supply up 3-4% due to project capex phases). AI-driven automation expected to reduce labor costs and lift margins to 12.5-13% in FY27. Direct expenses normalized ex-one-offs.
capex / expansion: Client project-related capex embedded in direct expenses; No major standalone corporate capex guided; Focus on AI technology investment and training rather than heavy asset buildup.
capital allocation: Dividend maintained at 30% (Rs. 1.50/share). Strategic conversion of Rs. 112 Cr subsidiary loans to equity to clean balance sheet and comply with regulations. Reinvestment in AI R&D and global delivery capabilities.
risks & watch-items: Government tender timing delays; Equipment price volatility (geopolitical impacts); Slow AI adoption in regulated sectors (Pharma); Execution risk on large Rs. 600 Cr+ bids; Regulatory approval timelines (RBI) for final audit clearance.
management quality / tone: Confident and transparent; Acknowledged past governance issues but emphasized full resolution of audit qualifications; Aggressive on AI transformation ('AI-first strategy'); Optimistic on FY27 government rebound despite Q4 softness.
non-obvious takeaways: The 'one-time' ECL provision artificially suppressed PAT while simultaneously creating a Rs. 21 Cr deferred tax asset that cushioned the bottom line; Management explicitly linked Q4 government slowdown to Iran-Israel war impacting equipment costs, causing them to walk away from specific bids rather than compete at loss-making prices; The conversion of loans to equity was framed as correcting the 'economic substance' of funds originally intended for US acquisitions.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

identity.name: ALLIED DIGITAL SERV. LTD
identity.industry: IT Services / Smart Governance & AI-Led Digital Transformation

hero.oneLiner: Allied Digital Services is a Mumbai-headquartered global IT services company operating as a Managed Service Provider and Master Systems Integrator across digital transformation, cybersecurity and digital engineering, with a presence in more than 70 countries.
hero.industry: IT Services / Smart Governance & AI-Led Digital Transformation

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Allied Digital Services is a Mumbai-headquartered global IT services company operating as a Managed Service Provider and Master Systems Integrator across digital transformation, cybersecurity and digital engineering, with a presence in more than 70 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ADSL began as one of India's early third-party IT infrastructure support providers and has evolved into a global IT consulting and services company delivering managed services, systems integration, digital workplace services, enterprise infrastructure transformation, cybersecurity, digital engineering, smart infrastructure and AI-Ops-led automation. It serves enterprises and government bodies across more than 70 countries, combining one-time Solutions (project-based implementations) with recurring annuity Services contracts that provide margin stability and customer retention. Its business model is shifting from conventional technology services toward platform-led, AI-enabled and outcome-oriented engagements, with roughly 20% of FY2025-26 revenue generated from smart city projects for government customers.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Services: +21% YoY (targeting 75-80% of mix for annuity visibility). Solutions: +17% YoY (strategic entry point). Enterprise Customers: +31% YoY. Government: -6% YoY (temporary delay due to war-induced equipment cost spikes and tender processing lags); expected rebound FY27.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Cloud and Infrastructure Services:** Cloud enablement across AWS, Azure, GCP and hybrid environments, Infrastructure modernisation, containerisation and microservices architecture, Disaster recovery and continuous infrastructure monitoring
- **Cybersecurity and Networking:** AIM 360 framework (prevention, detection, response, compliance), Security Operations Centres (SOC) with SIEM and SOAR, Zero Trust Architecture, SASE and endpoint detection and response, Identity and access management, ransomware protection and compliance frameworks, DPDP-readiness and OT security consulting
- **Digital Workspace Services:** 24x7 multi-channel, multi-lingual service desk operations, End-user computing, endpoint lifecycle management and global logistics, Cognitive support frameworks and analytics-driven workflow optimisation
- **AI Ops and Automation:** Digital Desk (AI-Ops-based ITSM/ESM no-code and low-code platform, rebranded from ADiTaaS in 2024), Digital Desk Bot Platform, 3A framework (Automation, Analytics, Agility), Agentic AI platform architecture, AI, machine learning, generative AI and robotic process automation (RPA), Low-code/no-code platforms, DevOps integration and enterprise applications
- **Digital Engineering Solutions:** Smart and Safe City solutions with integrated command and control centres, Intelligent building systems and operational technology (OT) integration, Real-time data platforms enabling predictive insights and automation, Computer vision, IoT and video analytics solutions

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Q4 new orders/renewals: Rs. 166 Cr. Key wins: Pune City Surveillance, Premier Pharma client, Deep Sea Oil Drilling managed services. Pending/Probable: Mumbai Govt contract (Rs. 150-200 Cr, announcement imminent), Western Railway rebid (Rs. 250 Cr total, expected July), Two Maharashtra state contracts (Rs. 600 Cr each), Noida Smart City.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: 20-25% YoY for FY27. Margins: Target 12.5-13% short-term, 15% long-term (driven by AI/Automation). Order inflow: Strong pipeline with major awards expected in Q2/Q3 FY27. Capex/Commissioning: Mumbai project (Rs. 150-200 Cr) to commission in 9 months followed by 5-year O&M.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Agentic AI architecture deployment reducing Level 1 support headcount by 20-25%; Smart City sensor/edge AI integration; Conversion of Solutions projects into 5-year Managed Services annuities; Geographic expansion in North America, Latin America, and Africa.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Enterprises have moved decisively to make AI operational, with agentic AI gaining rapid acceptance; enterprises invest in AI to reduce operating costs, improve end-user experience and strengthen decision-making
- Data sovereignty has become a core requirement, driving demand for local data centres, sovereign cloud environments and secure infrastructure for AI workloads - creating opportunities in data-centre build, cloud migration, technology operations and managed services
- Cybersecurity remains a priority as regulatory, operational and geopolitical risks increase; the Digital Personal Data Protection Act is expected to gain prominence as compliance deadlines approach, and OT security remains critical for manufacturing, FMCG and industrial businesses
- AI governance, data classification, data governance and data security are becoming standard requirements for application upgrades, while multi-cloud strategy, workload migration and cloud FinOps remain in demand
- Smart manufacturing is evolving from IoT-enabled monitoring to AI-driven autonomous operations (autonomous maintenance, closed-loop process optimisation, dynamic digital twins, flexible robotics), creating opportunities to extend digital engineering, computer vision and automation into industrial environments
- Government investment in digital governance, urban mobility, surveillance infrastructure and citizen-centric public services is a long-term opportunity; approximately 20% of FY2025-26 revenue came from smart city projects for government customers
- Growing opportunities across data centre modernisation, intelligent workplaces, operational technology integration, smart cities and digital infrastructure programmes are expected to remain important drivers of technology spending over the coming years
- Revenue mix shift toward enterprise-led and recurring managed services engagements improves revenue visibility, earnings stability and quality of growth; services-led engagements offer stronger retention and better operating leverage as relationships scale
- Margin levers cited: higher contribution from annuity-led managed services, greater utilisation of global delivery capabilities, and increasing adoption of automation, AI-led delivery frameworks and proprietary platforms
- Operating leverage is expected to improve progressively as the business scales beyond the ₹1,000 crore annualised revenue run-rate milestone
- Headwinds: the industry continues to face pricing pressure and customers remain focused on cost optimisation and cost control; FY2025-26 was challenging for India-based enterprises
- The financial year was challenging for the IT industry due to macroeconomic factors including the conflict in the Middle East, immigration-related challenges in the US and US tariff announcements
- One-time provisions in FY26 (expected credit losses, asset verification and other matters arising from the auditor-led review) were largely non-recurring; with these legacy matters substantially addressed, management expects future profitability to increasingly reflect operating strength rather than exceptional adjustments
- The Board's Report states the outlook for FY2026-27 remains positive with continued growth prospects for the IT industry in terms of underlying demand, and the Company foresees significant demand growth from its IT business
- Customers increasingly evaluate technology through operational resilience, uptime, automation, observability and business outcomes rather than implementation milestones, favouring partners able to manage the full digital infrastructure lifecycle
- Approximately ₹166 crore of orders and renewals were secured in the fourth quarter of FY26 alone, reflecting broad-based demand across digital transformation, infrastructure modernisation, managed services and AI-led solutions
- The Company continued to convert its order pipeline into active execution, improving future revenue visibility
- The Company enters FY2026-27 with a healthy pipeline of sizeable opportunities and expects several active deals to progress toward closure in the early quarters; the pipeline is expected to strengthen through the remainder of the year
- Key business wins during the year: a five-year end-user services contract from a leading global pharmaceutical company headquartered in Europe for its global operations
- A global end-user services contract from a leading New York-based fashion brand
- A three-year enterprise infrastructure services contract from a large premium investment-management company based in New York, USA
- A five-year subcontract to provide service desk and end-user field services for a well-known global offshore oil drilling company operating out of Texas, USA
- A five-year contract from a leading insurance company in India for end-user services, asset management, the Digital Desk platform and AI-enabled automation
- A five-year end-user service desk contract being delivered for a leading global IT services and consulting company
- A five-year comprehensive safe-city project, including a command centre, awarded by the Government of Maharashtra for an industrial zone - described as a significant safe-city order for industrial zones
- The Company successfully renewed key agreements and secured high-volume Smart/Safe City project contracts during the year

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Current EBITDA margin 11% pressured by one-time ECL provisions and elevated direct expenses (equipment supply up 3-4% due to project capex phases). AI-driven automation expected to reduce labor costs and lift margins to 12.5-13% in FY27. Direct expenses normalized ex-one-offs.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend maintained at 30% (Rs. 1.50/share). Strategic conversion of Rs. 112 Cr subsidiary loans to equity to clean balance sheet and comply with regulations. Reinvestment in AI R&D and global delivery capabilities.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: ADSL is an asset-light IT services business, and its expansion narrative is about footprint, partnerships, platforms and capability rather than plants or capacity. Geographic expansion is being pursued into newer geographies to increase addressable markets: the Company is evaluating partnerships in Japan, has established new partnerships in Mauritius to address opportunities in Mauritius and Africa, and continues to explore inorganic growth opportunities globally; the stated strategy also includes continued expansion across Japan and EMEA markets. Strategic global partnerships are being built with leading technology players - the recent addition of IBM as a strategic partner has already contributed to a large FMCG opportunity, with several additional opportunities being pursued through that collaboration. The sales and delivery engine has been expanded through senior sales leadership added in the US, a broader sales organisation, a new leader for the India managed services business, a refreshed digital presence and a global implementation of Salesforce for lead tracking, pipeline management and sales governance. Platform build-out continues around Digital Desk, the proprietary low-code/no-code enterprise service management platform, which now manages more than 6 million support tickets annually at an average first-time resolution rate of approximately 87%, while the AIM 360 cybersecurity framework has been extended through an assessment platform aligned with NIST-based industry controls and computer-vision applications are being expanded beyond smart cities into enterprise environments. Capability expansion includes training more than 100 key resources in AI, evaluating multiple AI platforms, assessing voice-to-text and text-to-voice technologies for virtual AI agents, and developing new business models and innovative pricing structures. The Company has defined a clear roadmap for the next three to five years aligned with its longer-term ambition to build a business ten times its current scale, and states that it strategically increased leverage by securing additional financing facilities during the year to fund its long-term project pipeline and accelerate group-level growth. No plant, capacity or rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this material.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and transparent; Acknowledged past governance issues but emphasized full resolution of audit qualifications; Aggressive on AI transformation ('AI-first strategy'); Optimistic on FY27 government rebound despite Q4 softness.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Four decades of operating history (42 years) with execution credentials in large-scale urban technology programmes, established through India's first smart city project - Pune Pimpri-Chinchwad City Surveillance
- Annuity-based recurring services model that supports customer stickiness, revenue visibility and margin stability over time
- Integrated full-lifecycle delivery across consulting, design, implementation, operations and governance, enabling cross-selling and participation in larger transformation programmes
- Global delivery footprint across 70+ countries and 20 offices with localised integration, giving local support at global standards
- Proprietary platforms and frameworks - Digital Desk (AI-Ops ITSM/ESM), the 3A framework and the AIM 360 security framework - plus an in-house agentic AI platform architecture
- Blue-chip customer base of 175 customers including 10 Fortune 100 companies
- Master Systems Integrator capability spanning command-centre implementation, multi-vendor integration and long-term operations support, a differentiator in government and public infrastructure programmes
- 3,000+ skilled professionals delivering worldwide

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Government tender timing delays; Equipment price volatility (geopolitical impacts); Slow AI adoption in regulated sectors (Pharma); Execution risk on large Rs. 600 Cr+ bids; Regulatory approval timelines (RBI) for final audit clearance.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 'one-time' ECL provision artificially suppressed PAT while simultaneously creating a Rs. 21 Cr deferred tax asset that cushioned the bottom line; Management explicitly linked Q4 government slowdown to Iran-Israel war impacting equipment costs, causing them to walk away from specific bids rather than compete at loss-making prices; The conversion of loans to equity was framed as correcting the 'economic substance' of funds originally intended for US acquisitions.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- A '10x growth strategy' targeting sustained annual growth of more than 25% over the long term, supported by a multi-pronged plan across geographic expansion, AI-first service transformation, data-centre opportunities, public-place technologies, computer vision, digital twins and global cybersecurity consulting
- Continue geographic expansion across Japan and EMEA markets
- Advance an AI-first strategy across service lines, enterprise AI, automation solutions and AI governance, including deployment of the Company's own agentic AI platform architecture and ready-to-deploy use cases
- Strengthen …

challenges.body:

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [New engagements] Entry into a new service line is claimed: an Enterprise Application Services engagement with "a leading NYSE-listed electronic design and test solutions company" covering ServiceNow, Jitterbit and Boomi, which "marks Allied Digital's entry into the Enterprise Application Services space".
- [New engagements] Other wins listed: end-to-end Workplace Services for a customer-owned (mutual) bank in Australia across Melbourne, Sydney and Adelaide; a turnkey System Integrator project from the Department of School Education, Government of Punjab for an Integrated Command and Control Centre; managed services for a Government of India organisation under the Ministry of Commerce; IT Asset Management for an international property consulting firm; and IT infrastructure support for "one of India's leading FMCG companies".
- [Renewals] "Renewed multiple strategic customer engagements across the pharmaceuticals, chemicals, real estate, BFSI, medical devices and retail design sectors" - the deck gives no contract values, durations or order book for any win or renewal.
- [FY26 one-off] The FY26 EBITDA figure of Rs. 112 cr is footnoted "* Excluding one-time provision of Rs. 36 Cr in FY26"; the deck does not say what the provision relates to.
- [Corporate history] Acquired EnPointe Global Services LLC in 2008 to expand US presence; converted to a public limited company and listed on BSE and NSE in 2007; the Chairman is described as leading the company "through Version 6.0".
